papers.title: Numerical simulation and experimental study on melt pool characteristics and temperature field evolution of Ti−15Mo alloy during selective laser melting

llm.why_not_core: The paper only models melt pool and temperature field during SLM of Ti-15Mo; it does not link porous architecture to stress shielding or stiffness matching, reports no mechanical/fatigue testing, and does not address surface roughness or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 厘清Ti−15Mo合金SLM成形中熔池行为与温度场演化规律。
summary_zh.method: 建立SLM热-流耦合数值模型并结合实验观测熔池形貌与温度分布。

summary_en.motivation: Understanding melt pool dynamics and thermal history is essential for controlling microstructure in SLM-fabricated Ti-15Mo biomedical alloy.
summary_en.method: A coupled thermal-fluid numerical model of the SLM process was developed and compared against experimental melt pool observations.
summary_en.result: The simulations and experiments jointly characterize how melt pool geometry and temperature field evolve with processing parameters.
summary_en.validation: Numerical predictions were validated against experimental SLM melt pool measurements.

papers.title: Beyond sacral slope change: a new lumbar flexion-based hip-spine classification for total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Aims The complex interplay between spinopelvic alignment and total hip arthroplasty (THA) outcomes has led to classification systems guiding acetabular component positioning. However, current systems rely heavily on sacral slope change (ΔSS) as a proxy for spinal mobility, despite emerging evidence questioning its accuracy. We introduce the Lumbar-Flexion Hip-Spine (LF-HS) classification (LF system), a novel system prioritizing true lumbar flexion (LF ≤ 20°) over ΔSS to assess spinal stiffness. This study compares the LF system with the established sacral-slope-based classification and evaluates its use in risk stratification and surgical planning. Methods In a retrospective cohort of 1,795 primary THA cases in 1,673 patients (mean age 66.1 years (23 to 94)), preoperative spinopelvic radiographs were analyzed to determine pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) mismatch, ΔSS, LF, and pelvic mobility parameters, including standing pelvic tilt (PT) and change in PT from flexed seated to standing (ΔPT). These were used as modifiers in the LF system. Patients were classified using both systems. We assessed group distributions, prevalence of spinopelvic risk factors, Hip User Index (HUI), and dislocation rates. Statistical comparisons included McNemar’s test and linear regression. Results The LF system identified 4% (n = 72) of patients as having spinal stiffness (LF ≤ 20°) compared with 41.9% (n = 753) using the SS system (ΔSS < 10%) (p < 0.001). LF-defined stiff spine groups showed significantly higher HUI scores ≥ 80%, indicating greater hip-dependent motion and dislocation risk. The two-year dislocation rate was 0.6%, lower than national benchmarks. The LF system demonstrated better age correlation and risk discrimination than the SS system. Conclusion The LF classification offers a more precise, mobility-driven approach to spinopelvic assessment in THA. Incorporating functional pelvic modifiers and replacing ΔSS with LF improves preoperative planning and may reduce complications, particularly dislocation. Adoption of the LF system may refine surgical decision-making towards a more individualized, biomechanics-based approach. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(11):1489–1497.
papers.first_author_affiliation: Lower Limb Fellow, Melbourne Orthopaedic Group (MOG), Melbourne, Australia

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文提出基于腰椎屈曲的髋-脊柱分类用于THA术前规划，与股骨柄应力遮挡、微动或骨-假体界面力学无关。
llm.why_not_core: This is a clinical radiographic classification study of spinopelvic alignment with no femoral stem biomechanics, no FEA, no stress shielding or micromotion quantification, and no bone-implant interface modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有髋-脊柱分类依赖骶骨倾斜角变化，可能无法准确反映脊柱僵硬程度。
summary_zh.method: 在1795例初次THA的回顾性队列中，用术前站立位与坐位X线测量PI-LL、ΔSS、腰椎屈曲及骨盆倾斜参数，构建LF-HS分类并与SS分类比较。

summary_zh.validation: 基于大样本临床影像与随访脱位率的回顾性统计验证。

summary_en.motivation: Existing hip-spine classifications rely on sacral slope change as a proxy for spinal mobility, which may misrepresent true spinal stiffness.
summary_en.method: In a retrospective cohort of 1,795 primary THA cases, preoperative spinopelvic radiographic parameters including PI-LL mismatch, sacral slope change, lumbar flexion, and pelvic tilt modifiers were used to construct and compare the Lumbar-Flexion Hip-Spine classification against the sacral-slope-based system.
summary_en.result: The LF system classified only 4% of patients as stiff-spined versus 41.9% under the SS system, with LF-defined stiff groups showing higher hip-dependent motion scores and better age correlation and risk discrimination, while the two-year dislocation rate was 0.6%.
summary_en.validation: Retrospective statistical analysis of clinical radiographic data and dislocation outcomes in a large patient cohort.

papers.title: A Koopman-PINN Framework for Epidemic Models: Parameter Inference and Forecasting
papers.abstract: We propose a Koopman-enhanced physics-informed neural network (K-PINN) framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models. This method combines Koopman operator theory and physics-informed learning. It maps epidemic states into a latent observable space where the dynamics evolve approximately linearly while satisfying the governing epidemic equations through automatic differentiation. This integration improves interpretability, parameter identifiability, and long-term predictive stability. We apply the proposed framework to a normalized SEIRSD epidemic model and evaluate it using synthetic monkeypox (Mpox) data and real-world datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden for the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Synthetic trajectories are generated using a structure-preserving, nonstandard finite difference scheme to ensure reliable training data. Numerical results demonstrate that K-PINN achieves more accurate parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting than classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches. These results suggest that K-PINN is an effective machine learning framework for epidemic modeling that can be extended to more complex systems.

papers.title: A human-centred framework for AI integration in the curriculum
papers.abstract: This paper reports ongoing work at La Trobe University to cultivate a shared understanding of effective artificial intelligence (AI) integration through the design of a human-centred framework for embedding AI literacies into teaching and learning. In response to conceptual ambiguity of AI curriculum integration, the Online Education Design team developed an operational definition positioning AI as infrastructure for active learning and the educator as the central decision-maker in the learning design process. This definition was translated into the AI-Informed Learning Design Framework, a four-step process, in which educators define the learning goal, select an AI pedagogical role, apply an AI Assessment Scale boundary check, then design learning activities that develop disciplinary knowledge and AI literacy. Supported by a four-level scaffolding model governing students' growing independence in AI use, the framework was piloted through two rounds, using a design-based research methodology. Feedback from Round one highlighted opportunities to refine the framework whilst also emphasising broader sector-wide tensions surrounding AI integration, including educators’ reluctance to use AI and concerns about the framing of some AI roles in teaching and learning. Early findings from the second round suggest improved educator engagement and a stronger understanding of the framework.

papers.title: Which design features of a digital simulation predict sustainability competency gains? Evidence from a large first-year business cohort
papers.abstract: Digital simulations offer experiential learning environments where students make consequential decisions under constraints. Yet little empirical evidence identifies which specific design features of these environments drive learning outcomes. This study examines a hotel carbon reduction simulation embedded in a first-year management unit (n=1,079 students, 190 teams) and investigates which of ten simulation design features predict gains in sustainability competencies. Students completed pre- and post-simulation surveys measuring 25 competency items aligned to an eight-domain sustainability competency framework (n=212 matched pairs), alongside a ten-item simulation evaluation scale (alpha=0.92). All self-reported 25 competency items improved significantly (composite d=0.62, p<.001). Regression analysis revealed that active learning engagement (beta=6.13, p<.001) was the strongest predictor of competency gains, followed by feedback quality and realistic scenarios. Full-cohort performance data showed 97.4% of teams maintained profitability while reducing emissions, with 45.8% clustering in a 'productive struggle zone' just below the target. These findings suggest that simulation designers should prioritise active engagement mechanisms and timely feedback over surface-level realism. Implications for the design of technology-enhanced experiential learning environments are discussed.

papers.title: Association between cementless femoral stem geometry and early aseptic loosening following primary total hip arthroplasty.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aseptic loosening is a significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA), particularly in geriatric patients with diminished bone quality. Femoral stem design in cementless primary THA for osteoarthritis (OA) plays a crucial role in mitigating this risk. This study examined the impact of stem geometry on early aseptic loosening. We hypothesised that single-taper (wedge) stems are associated with higher rates of early aseptic loosening. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 2952 cementless primary THA procedures at a single institution between November 2013 and December 2021. Patients ⩾ 65 years old who underwent primary THA for OA were included. Patients with preoperative diagnoses of fracture, avascular necrosis (AVN), or bone neoplasia, and those with periprosthetic fracture (PPF) within 90 days of index procedure were excluded. Femoral stems were categorised into 4 groups: (1) single-taper (wedge); (2A) collarless dual- and triple-taper; (2B) collared dual- and triple-taper; and (3) fit-and-fill. 2-year rates of femoral aseptic loosening as well as return to operating room (OR) were assessed. RESULTS: The study consisted of 1000 single-taper stems, 1185 collarless dual- and triple-taper stems, 213 collared dual- and triple-taper stems, and 554 fit-and-fill stems. Single-taper stems had significantly higher rates of aseptic loosening (0.8% vs. 0.2%) and overall return to the OR (2.6% versus 1.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Single-taper stems demonstrated higher rates of return to the OR and revision for femoral aseptic loosening during the 2-year postoperative period. Surgeons should consider these findings when selecting femoral stem designs for elderly patients who plan to undergo cementless primary THA.
